# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 3

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 2
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Bomb state: display reads 0. Light is green. Three wires: wire 1 is blue, wire 2 is green, wire 3 is red. Mute, I received your gestures but we have no shared code yet, so I could not read them. Blind, these colors are by position, left to right as wires 1, 2, 3.

Deaf has given me the bomb's visual state: display reads 0, light is green, wires 1=blue, 2=green, 3=red. That's the raw perception. But I still don't know the rule — that's Mute's manual. Mute apparently gestured something to Deaf (which Deaf couldn't decode), and I haven't heard Mute's manual rule yet.

I need the manual's rule for display=0, light=green, and these wire colors. I'll speak to Mute asking for exactly that, and gesture nothing meaningful (no shared code). Actually, I should just ask Mute for the rule.

Let me speak to Mute with the state Deaf gave me and request the rule.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Blind here. Deaf reports: display 0, light green, wires 1 blue, 2 green, 3 red. I need the manual's rule: given display 0, light green, and these colors, which single wire position do I cut? Give me the number 1, 2, or 3.")
wait()
```

TURN 3
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Update: light is now BLUE, not green. Display still 0. Wires unchanged: 1 blue, 2 green, 3 red. Mute, we need a code. Proposal: gesture the wire to cut as ? for wire 1, ? for wire 2, ? for wire 3. I will relay your answer to Blind by speech.

Deaf has updated: light is now BLUE (not green), display still 0, wires unchanged. Deaf proposes a gesture code to relay Mute's answer to me — but wait, Deaf can't hear Mute (Mute can't speak). Mute gestures; Deaf sees gestures. So Deaf CAN see Mute's gestures. The relay works: Mute gestures the wire number, Deaf reads it and speaks it to me.

But there's a problem: I never received Mute's manual rule directly. Mute's speech reaches me (I receive Mute's speech). Actually — Mute can't speak at all. So Mute can only gesture. I can't see gestures. So the ONLY way Mute's manual knowledge reaches me is through Deaf relaying it by speech. Deaf is the bridge.

So I'm dependent on Deaf reading Mute's gestures correctly. Deaf proposed a code: gesture symbol for wire 1, another for wire 2, another for wire 3. That's a good idea — I should endorse it and ask Mute to gesture the answer.

I speak to Mute (my speech reaches Mute). I can tell Mute the code is fine and ask for the answer. Also Deaf's proposal needs Mute to agree. Let me speak to Mute endorsing the code and giving the state.

Also I could gesture to Deaf to confirm — but gestures carry no words and Deaf can't decode. Better to speak to Mute, and let Mute gesture to Deaf, Deaf speaks to me.

Let me speak to Mute.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Blind here. Deaf's code is good: gesture one symbol to mean the wire to cut. State now: display 0, light BLUE, wires 1 blue, 2 green, 3 red. Read the manual and gesture the correct wire position to Deaf. Deaf will speak it to me and I will cut.")
wait()
```

TURN 4
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Blind: cut wire 2. That is the green wire, the middle one. Display is 0 and light is blue. Mute, if wire 2 is wrong, gesture ? now to stop.

Deaf relays: cut wire 2 (green, middle). Display 0, light blue. Deaf offers Mute a chance to veto with a gesture. But I don't know if Mute confirmed — Deaf is asserting the answer came from the manual. I have to trust the chain: Mute read the manual, gestured, Deaf decoded.

However, I should be cautious. The rule for "display 0, light blue" — I have no way to verify. Deaf says cut wire 2. Mute hasn't objected (no veto reported). This is the best information I have.

But wait — should I wait for Mute's confirmation? Deaf already framed it as the answer and offered a veto. If Mute had vetoed, Deaf would presumably have relayed it. The state is consistent. I'll act.

Actually, let me reconsider: is there risk? A wrong action detonates. I have exactly one shot. The chain is: Mute reads manual → gestures → Deaf decodes → tells me. Deaf's decode could be wrong. But I have nothing better. Deaf explicitly tied "wire 2" to "the green wire, the middle one" — a concrete, checkable description, which reduces ambiguity (Deaf isn't just guessing a number, they're describing a specific wire).

I'll cut wire 2.

```
act(op="cut", position=2)
```
